title: Give a partner three fields, for three days, and take them back
summary: A shared record is narrower than a pseudonym in every dimension: only the named fields, only until expiry, revocable at any moment - and a consent withdrawal revokes it for good, so a link that was handed out never quietly comes back.

steps.label: A person with more fields than the partner should see
steps.note: The blob holds a tier, an IBAN and contact details. The partner needs one of them.

steps.label: Mint a share for exactly one field
steps.note: The share carries a purpose, and minting it requires the creator to be able to READ those fields itself - a share cannot leak what its creator may not see. The partner never gets a credential.

steps.label: The partner reads the share
steps.note: One unguessable UUID, one field. Every fetch is audited with the partner label, so a leak is attributable to whoever was handed the link.

steps.label: The person withdraws consent for that purpose
steps.note: Consent is re-checked at every fetch, not only when the share was minted - otherwise a link handed out a second before the withdrawal would keep working until it expired.

steps.label: The same link stops answering
steps.note: Withdrawn, expired, revoked and never-existed all look identical from outside: one 404. The partner learns that their link no longer works, and nothing about why.

steps.label: Consent restored - but the link does NOT come back
steps.note: The withdrawal did not mute the share, it REVOKED it. Re-granting consent restores the person's data flows in general, and deliberately does not resurrect a link that was already handed out: the partner has to be given a new one, which is a decision someone makes again.

steps.label: Still 404 - revocation is not temporary
steps.note: This is the step worth pausing on. A share that came back to life by itself, because a consent flag flipped twice, would be a share nobody can reason about.

steps.label: Mint a fresh share for the partner
steps.note: The ordinary way forward: a new UUID, a new expiry, a new decision on the audit chain.

assert.message: a replacement share is a new link, never the revoked one revived

steps.label: The new link answers
steps.note: Same field, same purpose, different link - and the old one is still dead.

steps.label: Revoke it deliberately
steps.note: The ordinary end of a share: the partnership ends, the link dies, immediately - no waiting for the TTL.

steps.label: And it stays dead
steps.note: Revocation is not a soft flag the reader may ignore: the fetch path checks it before it decrypts anything.
